diagnostic_evidence.quote: In this section, we provide general bounds on the growth of the condition number as columns are added to a matrix without making any assumptions about the matrix or the added column.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof writes the Gram matrix of [B,(x+y)γ] as blkdiag(BᵀB,1)+[[0,γBᵀy],[γyᵀB,γ²‖x+y‖²]], whose corner entry is 1+γ²‖x+y‖² and hence which is not the Gram matrix, and then replaces λmax and λmin of the block-diagonal part by σ²max(B) and σ²min(B). Those replacements require σ²min(B) ≤ γ²‖x+y‖² ≤ σ²max(B), which the statement does not assume. The lower bound on σmin is therefore false: for B=e₁∈R^{2×1}, x=0.1e₂, y=0, γ=1 the hypothesis x∈span(B)^⊥ holds and κ([B,b])=10 while the displayed right-hand side is √1.01; for B=diag(2,3) with a zero third row, x=e₃, y=0, γ=1 one gets κ([B,b])=3 against √2.5. In addition the denominator 2σ²min(B)+γ²‖x+y‖²−√(γ⁴‖x+y‖⁴+4γ²‖Bᵀy‖²) can be nonpositive (e.g. B=diag(0.1,1) with a zero third row, x=0, y=e₁, γ=1 gives a negative denominator), so the bound is not even a real number there.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate item (1) with max{σ²max(B),γ²‖x+y‖²} and min{σ²min(B),γ²‖x+y‖²) in place of σ²max(B) and σ²min(B) (equivalently add σ²min(B) ≤ γ²‖x+y‖² ≤ σ²max(B), which covers the unit-norm application), and restrict the claim to parameter values for which the denominator is positive.
issues.overall_effect: Item (1) of thm:cool is unreliable in its advertised assumption-free regime, and the displayed quantity can be non-real; item (2), which is derived from item (1), is unreliable as well. No other labelled result cites thm:cool.
issues.title: thm:cool item (1) is false: extreme-eigenvalue estimates silently assume an unstated normalized regime
issues.why_classification: The same Weyl argument with the corrected block-extreme terms is a valid bound of identical shape and reduces to the printed formula in the normalized regime, so the advertised assumption-free scope survives; but the bound must be weakened (or its regime restricted) over part of the stated parameter range, which is more than a routine local edit.

issues.failure_explanation: From ‖Bᵀy‖/‖x+y‖ ≤ (ε²−1)/4 one only gets 1+4‖Bᵀy‖²/‖x+y‖² ≤ 1+(ε²−1)²/4, and 1+(ε²−1)²/4 ≤ ε² holds exactly when 1 ≤ ε² ≤ 5. For ε>√5 the inference used in the proof is invalid (ε=3 and ‖Bᵀy‖/‖x+y‖=2 satisfy the hypothesis but give √17>3). Independently, the right-hand side κ(B)√(1+f(B,ε)) need not be real: the hypothesis forces ε ≥ 1 while f(B,ε) has positive numerator and denominator 2σ²min(B)+1−ε, so for ε > 2σ²min(B)+1 one gets 1+f(B,ε)<0 (B=e₁∈R^{2×1}, x=0.1e₂, y=0 satisfies the hypothesis for every ε ≥ 1, and at ε=4 one has 1+f = −7).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis to ‖Bᵀy‖₂/‖x+y‖₂ ≤ √(ε²−1)/2 (or keep the printed hypothesis and require 1 ≤ ε ≤ √5), and restrict the claim to 2σ²min(B)+1−ε > 0 (or state the bound only when 1+f(B,ε) ≥ 0).
issues.overall_effect: The guarantee κ([B,(x+y)/‖x+y‖]) ≤ κ(B)√(1+f(B,ε)) fails for ε>√5 and is meaningless for ε ≥ 2σ²min(B)+1; it holds at most in a restricted ε-range under a strengthened hypothesis, and it is additionally unreliable through its derivation from item (1).
issues.title: thm:cool item (2): the ε-hypothesis does not imply the inequality used and the bound need not be real
issues.why_classification: Both corrections are local hypothesis/range restrictions that leave the bound formula and its conclusion intact, but the quantifier over ε must be narrowed and a hypothesis strengthened, so part of the advertised parameter range is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The α→0 limit of the integral definition is Γ(M,β²/2)/Γ(M), i.e. P(χ²_{2M} > β²); the printed Γ(M,β²)/Γ(M) is the survival function of χ²_{2M} evaluated at 2β². Consequently every use of Q^{ma}_M(0,·) is numerically wrong: e.g. for m=2, σ=1, X=0 Theorem thm:Malcum-Bessel/Corollary cor:golden2 give P(‖Y‖₂ ≤ 1) = 1−e^{−1} = 0.632 instead of the correct 1−e^{−1/2} = 0.393.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Γ(M,β²)/Γ(M) by Γ(M,β²/2)/Γ(M) in Definition def:marc-func, which is the α→0 limit of the integral definition already printed in the same definition.
issues.overall_effect: All statements that evaluate Q^{ma}_M(0,·) — Corollary cor:golden2, Corollary cor:golden3, and Theorem thm:Malcum-Bessel in the degenerate case X=0 — yield wrong probabilities, and the intermediate Marcum-Q values quoted in the proof of Theorem thm:noise-ls are wrong too.
issues.title: def:marc-func: the α=0 value of the generalized Marcum-Q function is wrong
issues.why_classification: A single local formula correction restores consistency with the definition's own integral form and with the distribution used in the proofs; every claim, method and scope item survives unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $X\in \mathbb{R}^m$ and $Y$ is a random vector such that $Y_i$s are i.i.d. and $Y_i \sim N(0,\sigma^2)$, then:
This result follows directly from Theorem~\ref{thm:Malcum-Bessel} by setting $X=0$ and applying basic probability theory.

issues.failure_explanation: Only marginal normality is assumed, but the proof invokes Theorem thm:Malcum-Bessel, which needs i.i.d. components, to conclude that ‖Y‖₂/σ is chi with m degrees of freedom. Without independence the identity is false: if Y₁=…=Y_m=Z with Z∼N(0,σ²), then P(‖Y‖₂ ≤ ε) = P(|Z| ≤ ε/√m), which differs from 1−Q^{ma}_{m/2}(0,ε/σ) for m>1.

failure_location.quote: If $Y\in \mathbb{R}^m$ is a random vector such that $Y_i \sim N(0,\sigma^2)$, then:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that the components of Y are i.i.d. N(0,σ²), matching the hypothesis of Theorem thm:Malcum-Bessel that the proof applies.
issues.overall_effect: The norm-tail identity is unreliable for Gaussian vectors with dependent components; the corollary is valid only for i.i.d. noise.
issues.title: cor:golden2 omits the independence hypothesis needed for the norm distribution
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard local hypothesis already present in the invoked theorem restores the claim with no change to method, conclusion or scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let \( Q \) be an orthonormal \( m \times n \) matrix with \( m \geq n \)

issues.failure_explanation: The exponent (m−n)/2 presumes rank(P_B^⊥)=m−n, i.e. that B has full column rank; no such hypothesis is stated. For rank(B)=r<n the correct factor is (m−r)/2. If B is the m×n zero matrix, then P_B^⊥=I and P(‖Y‖₂ ≤ ε) = 1−Q^{ma}_{m/2}(0,ε/σ), which differs from the displayed value for every n ≥ 1.

failure_location.quote: Let \( B \) be an \( m \times n \) matrix with \( m \geq n \), and \( Y \in \mathbb{R}^m \) be a random vector with i.i.d. components \( Y_i \sim N(0, \sigma^2) \). Then:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis rank(B)=n, i.e. that an orthonormal basis of span(B) has n columns, which is the case in which Theorem thm:projected-noise applies.
issues.overall_effect: The stated probability identity fails for rank-deficient B; it is valid only in the full-column-rank case used later in the least-squares section.
issues.title: cor:golden3 needs full column rank of B
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local rank condition preserves the identity and its scope; no argument or construction changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The probability that the norm of \( X + P_{Q}^{\perp}(Y) \) exceeds \( \varepsilon \) is given by \( \mathcal{Q}^{ma}_{(m-n)/2}\left(\frac{\|X\|_2}{\sigma},\frac{\varepsilon}{\sigma}\right) \)

issues.failure_explanation: The assumptions of Theorem thm:projected-noise leave X arbitrary in span(Q)^⊥, and the probability P(‖X+P_Q^⊥Y‖₂ > ε) is minimal at X=0. With the printed σ = 2^{−8} and ε = 1/10 the threshold is ε/σ = 25.6, so at X=0 the probability equals P(χ_{m−n} > 25.6); for m−n = 100 this is essentially zero (χ²₁₀₀ would have to exceed 655.36, against a mean of 100), not at least 0.9734. The stated lower bound is therefore false at X=0 for any codimension of the printed order; it only becomes plausible if ‖X‖₂ is itself comparable to ε or if the codimension is several hundred.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the constant: restrict the regime (a codimension of order (ε/σ)², or a lower bound on ‖X‖₂ comparable to ε) or weaken the numerical bound, keeping the qualitative illustration only in that regime.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised conclusion that the noise makes ‖X+P_Q^⊥Y‖₂ exceed 1/10 with probability at least 0.9734 for tall matrices is unreliable: at the printed noise level the perturbation norm is about σ√(m−n), far below the threshold for m−n of the stated order and X=0.
issues.title: cor:added-1: the numerical probability bound is false for the printed parameters
issues.why_classification: The claim must be restated with a different parameter regime or an added hypothesis on ‖X‖₂ and the constant re-evaluated, which is more than a one-symbol edit; it is a contained change that leaves a recognizably comparable numerical illustration.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $Z_1 \sim \chi^2_n$, $Z_2 \sim \chi'^2_{m-n}\left(\frac{\|X\|_2^2}{\sigma^2}\right)$, therefore, by Chapter 6, equation 40 of \cite{patnaik1949non}, we have:

issues.failure_explanation: Z₁ and Z₂ are defined as norms, so Z₁/σ is chi and Z₂/σ is noncentral chi; the claim Z₁∼χ²_n, Z₂∼χ'²_{m−n} is false, and the noncentral F applies to (Z₂²/(m−n))/(Z₁²/n), not to (Z₂/(m−n))/(Z₁/n). The event ‖r‖₂ ≥ (1+(ε₁/ε₂)²)^{−1/2} is {Z₂/Z₁ ≥ ε₂/ε₁} = {(Z₂²/(m−n))/(Z₁²/n) ≥ nε₂²/((m−n)ε₁²)}, so the probability is F'_{m-n,n}(nε₂²/((m−n)ε₁²); ‖X‖²/σ²). The printed argument nε₂/((m−n)ε₁) is not a monotone transform of the correct one: the left-hand side depends on (ε₁/ε₂)² while the printed right-hand side depends on ε₂/ε₁, and the two agree only at ε₁=ε₂.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Square the ratio in the argument of F' (use nε₂²/((m−n)ε₁²)) and correct the distribution statements for Z₁ and Z₂; equivalently, re-parametrize the left threshold as (1+ε₁/ε₂)^{−1/2} and keep the printed F-argument.
issues.overall_effect: The exact probability identity of Theorem thm:noise-ls is quantitatively wrong; the probability expressions of Corollary cor-main and Corollary cor:added-2, which quote the same F-threshold, are wrong with it.
issues.title: thm:noise-ls: the noncentral-F threshold is wrong (the squared ratio is required)
issues.why_classification: Either correction is a local formula change that preserves the exact-identity form, the scope and the use of the result; no new lemma or construction is needed, and the same local fix repairs the dependent probability expressions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume \( B \in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R}) \), \( c\in \mathbb{R}^{m} \), \( \gamma \in \mathbb{R} \), \( B = QR \), and \( \alpha=1+\gamma^2\|c\|_2^2 \). Then:

issues.failure_explanation: The proof uses σmax(diag(R,γ)) = max{σmax(R),γ} and σmin(diag(R,γ)) = min{σmin(R),γ}, valid only for γ ≥ 0; for γ<0 the correct quantities involve |γ|. Since the statement quantifies over γ∈R it is false as printed: with B=[1], c=1, γ=−2 one has σmax([B,cγ]) = σmax([1,−2]) = √5 while max{σmax(B),γ}·σmax([Q,c]) = 1·√2 = √2. The same sign error makes the second expression in item (3), max{κ(B),‖B‖₂/γ, γ‖B†‖₂}κ([Q,c]), false for γ<0, where it collapses to κ(B)κ([Q,c]): for B=I₂, c=e₁, γ=−2 this gives √2 against the true κ([B,cγ]) = √5.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace γ by |γ| in max{σmax(B),γ}, min{σmin(B),γ} and in max{κ(B),‖B‖₂/γ, γ‖B†‖₂} (or restrict the theorem to γ>0, as the cited Theorem 2.3 does).
issues.overall_effect: Items (1) and the second bound of item (3) of thm:min-max-cond are false for negative γ, and item (2) is vacuous there; the positive-γ applications are unaffected once |γ| is used.
issues.title: thm:min-max-cond items (1)–(3): the scaling parameter must be |γ| (bounds fail for γ<0)
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol sign correction restores every bound with no loss of scope or strength; no argument, construction or rate changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The two prefactors multiply different quantities: max{κ(B),‖B‖₂,‖B†‖₂}·κ([Q,cγ]) and max{κ(B),‖B‖₂/γ, γ‖B†‖₂}·κ([Q,c]). Since [Q,cγ] = [Q,c]·diag(I,γ) one has κ([Q,cγ]) ≠ κ([Q,c]) in general, so the asserted equality is false: for B=I₂, c=e₁, γ=2 the left expression equals κ([I,2e₁]) = √5 whereas the right one equals 2·κ([I,e₁]) = 2√2. Moreover the proof derives only the second expression (items (1) and (2) divided), so the first expression is asserted but never established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the '=' and state the two bounds separately, adding the missing one-line justification of the first (κ([B,cγ]) = κ([Q,cγ]·diag(R,1)) ≤ κ([Q,cγ])·max{σmax(R),1}/min{σmin(R),1}).
issues.overall_effect: Item (3) asserts a false identity and one of its two bounds is unproven; Theorem lm:cond-ls cites exactly that unproven bound when it concludes κ([B,cγ]) ≤ κ(B)κ([Q,cγ]).
issues.title: thm:min-max-cond item (3): false equality between two different condition-number bounds
issues.why_classification: Both bounds are true once stated separately, and the missing step is a routine submultiplicativity estimate; no claim, scope or rate is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: Equation (2.8) of the cited theorem expresses κ([Q,cγ]) through the least-squares residual of the unscaled column, ‖r‖ = min_z‖c−Bz‖, with α = 1+γ²‖c‖₂². Theorem lm:cond-ls instead defines ‖r‖₂ = min_z‖cγ−Bz‖ = |γ|·min_z‖c−Bz‖ and inserts that quantity into the same formula. The statement is therefore false: for B=e₁∈R^{2×1} (unit column), c = e₁+0.01e₂, γ=2 one has κ([B,cγ]) = 250 while the displayed right-hand side is ≈125. For γ>1 the radicand α²−4γ²‖r‖₂² can be negative (B=e₁, c=e₂, γ=2 gives 25−64), and for γ<0 the right-hand side is negative although κ>0, since the formula requires γ>0 as in the cited theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either define ‖r‖₂ as min_z‖c−Bz‖ and require γ>0 as in the cited theorem, or keep the printed definition and replace the bound by κ(B)·(α+√(α²−4‖r‖₂²))/(2‖r‖₂); the two repairs give the same statement.
issues.overall_effect: The upper bound on κ([B,cγ]) is unreliable for γ≠1, where it can be violated by an unbounded factor or be non-real/negative; Corollary cor:cond-ls and the later corollaries, which use only γ=1 where the two residual definitions coincide, keep their form.
issues.title: lm:cond-ls inserts the residual of the scaled column into Strakoš's formula
issues.why_classification: The source itself displays both consistent readings (through Theorem thm:strak), so two local equivalent repairs exist, each preserving the bound's form, strength and scope with no new argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follows by recognizing that $\frac{1+\sqrt{1 -  \|r\|_2^2}}{ \|r\|_2}$ is a decreasing function of $\|r\|_2$, and then applying Corollary \ref{cor:cond-ls} and Theorem \ref{thm:noise-ls}.

Assume \( B \) is an \( m \times n \) full rank matrix \( (m > n) \) and \( X\in \mathrm{span}(B^{\perp}) \subset \mathbb{R}^m= \mathrm{span}(B^{\perp})\bigoplus \mathrm{span}(B) \) and \( Y \) is a random vector such that \( Y_i \)'s are i.i.d. with \( Y_i\sim N(0,\sigma^2) \). Then for all \( \varepsilon_1 \geq 0 \) and \( \varepsilon_2 > 0 \), we have:

issues.failure_explanation: The quantity q is never defined in the statement (only B, X and Y appear); the intended object is q = (X+Y)/‖X+Y‖₂, for which the ‖r‖₂ of Theorem thm:noise-ls equals min_z‖q−Bz‖₂. With that reading, evaluating the decreasing function (1+√(1−u²))/u at the threshold u = 1/√(1+(ε₁/ε₂)²) gives κ([B,q]) ≤ (√(1+(ε₁/ε₂)²)+ε₁/ε₂)κ(B), not ε₁√(1+(ε₁/ε₂)²)κ(B). The printed factor is not scale invariant in (ε₁,ε₂) although the probability depends only on their ratio, and it can be below 1: with ε₁=ε₂=0.001 and κ(B)=1 the corollary asserts κ([B,q]) ≤ 0.00142 with probability F'_{m-n,n}(n/(m−n);‖X‖²/σ²) > 0, although κ([B,q]) ≥ 1 always.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the corollary with q := (X+Y)/‖X+Y‖₂ and with the correct factor √(1+(ε₁/ε₂)²)+ε₁/ε₂ obtained by evaluating the monotone function at the threshold.
issues.overall_effect: The high-probability condition-number guarantee of Corollary cor-main is false as stated (it asserts bounds that can be below 1) and is not a well-formed claim until q is defined; Corollary cor:added-2, which multiplies the same factor over the iterations, inherits the defect.
issues.title: cor-main states a bound its argument does not give, and never defines q
issues.why_classification: The repair is a restatement of the bound with a larger, scale-invariant factor plus a missing definition; the qualitative guarantee (κ([B,q]) within a factor depending only on ε₁/ε₂ of κ(B), with the stated probability) survives as a recognizably comparable result, but the printed quantitative bound must be weakened.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and $a_i \in span(\hat{Q}[:,1:i-1])^{\perp}$ and $e_i$ is a random vector in $\mathbb{R}^m$ with $e_i$ i.i.d. and $e_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2 I)$.

issues.failure_explanation: At iteration i the new column is orthogonalized against Q̂[:,1:i−1], a matrix with i−1 columns, so Corollary cor-main applies with n = i−1 and yields F'_{m-i+1,i-1}((i−1)ε₂/((m-i+1)ε₁); ‖a_i‖²/σ²) (with the squared ratio once Theorem thm:noise-ls is corrected). The printed F'_{m-i,i}(iε₂/((m−i)ε₁);·) is cor-main's expression evaluated at n = i, an off-by-one substitution that differs at every iteration. In addition the event E_i is written with κ(Q̂[:,i]) and κ(Q̂[:,i−1]), which under the paper's notation A[:,j] are single columns (condition number 1), so the telescoping conclusion is not justified as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Substitute n = i−1 in the cor-main expression at step i (giving F'_{m-i+1,i-1} with threshold (i−1)ε_{2,i}/((m-i+1)ε_{1,i}) and its squared variant) and write the iterates as Q̂[:,1:i] in the definition of E_i.
issues.overall_effect: The probability attached to the product bound on κ(Q̂) is wrong at every iteration, so the final high-probability guarantee of Corollary cor:added-2 does not hold with the stated probability.
issues.title: cor:added-2: wrong degrees of freedom in the per-iteration noncentral-F probability
issues.why_classification: An index correction plus a notational fix restores the union-bound argument and the product guarantee with the same form and scope; no new construction or lemma is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This offers a new perspective on understanding MGS without the usual restrictions on machine precision or the number of columns in the input matrix.
We consider the case where orthogonalization might not be perfect, but normalization is assumed to be accurate.
orthogonalization is subject to noise. Meaning $\hat{q}_i = \frac{a_i + e_i}{\|a_i + e_i\|_2}$

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims specific implications for MGS and a way to understand MGS without the usual restrictions on machine precision or on the number of columns. The paper states nothing about MGS: its only algorithmic content, Corollary cor:added-2, treats a generic QR run in which normalization is exact and the orthogonalization error is an assumed i.i.d. Gaussian vector of variance σ². No result derives that model from MGS's finite-precision rounding errors, relates σ to machine precision u or to the column count, or bounds MGS's actual loss of orthogonality; everything obtained is conditional on the assumed noise model.

failure_location.quote: We investigated how the condition number can grow due to noise in the orthogonalization step with specific implications for the Modified Gram-Schmidt (MGS) algorithm.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Narrow the conclusion to what is proved: a probabilistic bound on κ(Q̂) for a stylized model of noisy orthogonalization with exact normalization, without MGS-specific claims or claims about removing machine-precision and column-count restrictions.
issues.overall_effect: The headline application claim of the conclusion is unsupported; only the conditional Gaussian-noise model of a noisy orthogonalization step is established, not any consequence specific to MGS or free of machine-precision/column-count restrictions.
issues.title: Conclusion claims MGS-specific consequences that no result establishes
issues.why_classification: The repair withdraws an advertised application promise but requires no change to any formal result; the model-level guarantee remains a recognizably comparable conclusion, so the loss is limited to the over-claimed scope.
